prerequisites.gpu: NVIDIA GPU with at least 8GB VRAM is ideal. A GPU is not strictly required, but on CPU training and evaluation are roughly 10x slower for ResNets. NVIDIA driver must be installed first; CUDA is usually obtained via the PyTorch install. Apple M-chip GPUs are used automatically by PyTorch via Metal.
notes: As of v3.0+ the default engine is PyTorch. TensorFlow is opt-in via the deeplabcut[tf] extra and will be deprecated by v3.2 at the latest.
Native Windows GPU support for TensorFlow ended after TF 2.10; maintainers recommend WSL for Windows users who need TF GPU support.

installation.recommended: conda environment built from the supplied DEEPLABCUT.yaml

methods.name: Docker
steps: Images at docker.io/deeplabcut/deeplabcut. Linux hosts only.

installation.verify: python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"  # expect True on CUDA GPU

troubleshooting.question: Windows: model downloads fail or symlink errors when videos are not copied into the project folder.
troubleshooting.answer: Open the terminal / cmd / Anaconda prompt as Administrator (right click, 'Run as administrator').

troubleshooting.question: Errors when creating new videos, particularly after a Windows update.
troubleshooting.answer: Re-install ffmpeg. On Ubuntu: sudo apt install ffmpeg.

troubleshooting.question: 'import deeplabcut' picks up the wrong version.
troubleshooting.answer: If you git-cloned the repo and are working inside that folder, the import resolves to the local folder rather than the installed PyPI package.

troubleshooting.question: TensorFlow and PyTorch fight over competing CUDA-toolkit dependencies.
troubleshooting.answer: Use the pinned extras (tf-cu11 / tf-cu12), which cap the PyTorch version to match the CUDA requirement. As a fallback on Linux, let TF install its own CUDA libraries with pip install 'tensorflow[and-cuda]==<version>' — note this may break PyTorch functionality.

troubleshooting.question: Installing into the base environment causes package conflicts.
troubleshooting.answer: Maintainers explicitly warn against system-wide / base-environment installs; a system-wide install overwrites conflicting packages and degrades over time. Use a conda or uv managed environment.

troubleshooting.question: Fresh Ubuntu install fails to build dependencies.
troubleshooting.answer: Run: sudo apt-get install gcc python3-dev

compatibility_notes: Data labelled in v2.x is compatible with v3+ and the PyTorch engine; no workflow change required.
A model trained on one camera may not generalise to another; maintainers recommend the same camera for training and inference.

verification.notes: License not stated on the installation page; left unset rather than guessed.

prerequisites.python: 3.11, 3.12, 3.13. Python 3.14 is not yet tested or supported.
prerequisites.gpu: GPU-accelerated training on NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon. Other architectures (e.g. AMD GPUs, older Macs) are NOT supported and may fail or behave unexpectedly. CPU mode works but training is slower.
notes: SLEAP 1.5+ uses uv; older versions used conda (see legacy docs).
The GUI can be installed alone for labeling; sleap-nn is the training/inference backend and needs matching PyTorch/CUDA versions.
Maintainers strongly recommend installing into a fresh environment when updating, since dependency versions change.

methods.name: uv
steps: Install uv: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh (macOS/Linux) or powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex" (Windows)

methods.name: conda / miniforge
steps: Create and activate a dedicated environment, then use the pip install commands inside it

troubleshooting.question: Something is wrong and I don't know where to start.
troubleshooting.answer: Run `sleap doctor` and check the output for errors. This is the documented first step.

troubleshooting.question: `--torch-backend` is not recognized.
troubleshooting.answer: Update uv to the latest version: uv self update. The flag requires uv 0.9.20+.

troubleshooting.question: uv installs Python 3.14, which SLEAP does not support.
troubleshooting.answer: Pin a supported version: add --python 3.13 to the install command.

troubleshooting.question: Commands fail after a uv-based install.
troubleshooting.answer: Prefix commands with `uv run` so they execute inside the correct virtual environment.

troubleshooting.question: Old Anaconda install resolves dependencies very slowly or fails.
troubleshooting.answer: Set the libmamba solver in the base environment: conda update -n base conda; conda install -n base conda-libmamba-solver; conda config --set solver libmamba.

troubleshooting.question: Import errors after changing GPUs or updating CUDA drivers.
troubleshooting.answer: Force a clean reinstall — the docs call this out specifically for the case of updated CUDA drivers or changed GPUs.

verification.notes: Confirmed from official docs snippets rather than a full page fetch. Talmo Lab is also named as a collaborator on R34DA059513 in the blitz transcript.

prerequisites.python: >= 3.10 (MNE 1.11+ / 1.12+). MNE 0.17 was the last release supporting Python 2.7.
optional: FreeSurfer (converting structural MRI to scalp/skull/cortical surface models)
notes: Anaconda Inc. changed their terms of service in March 2024; the MNE docs recommend Miniforge or the pre-built MNE installer if you are unsure whether your usage requires a paid license.
The pip-installed core supports 2D plotting but NOT 3D visualization.

installation.recommended: pre-built MNE-Python standalone installer for users new to Python

methods.name: conda
steps: Create a dedicated env; installing into its own env keeps 3D plotting dependencies in sync

troubleshooting.question: `mne` command not found / import fails after install.
troubleshooting.answer: The environment containing MNE-Python is probably not active. Run `conda activate mne` and retry. To activate automatically: echo conda activate mne >> ~/.bashrc (bash) or >> ~/.zprofile (zsh).

troubleshooting.question: HDF5 I/O functions fail (read_raw_eeglab, SourceMorph.save, etc.).
troubleshooting.answer: These require extra packages beyond the core pip install; install them into the same environment to unlock HDF5 support.

troubleshooting.question: Spyder console will not start against an MNE environment.
troubleshooting.answer: spyder-kernels is missing — install the required version into the conda environment.

troubleshooting.question: Where do I get help for an install problem not covered here?
troubleshooting.answer: The docs point to the Advanced Setup page first, then the MNE Forum (https://mne.discourse.group/) as the recommended venue for install troubleshooting.

verification.notes: Some troubleshooting items are sourced from an older docs version (0.23) where the current page no longer restates them; version noted in each source_url.

troubleshooting.question: Behaviour keys from an old project no longer match.
troubleshooting.answer: Keys are case-sensitive. For projects created with BORIS < v7, use the 'Convert keys to lower case' tool.

troubleshooting.question: BORIS pauses and asks which behaviour to record.
troubleshooting.answer: This is expected behaviour when a keypress is ambiguous across the ethogram; select the intended behaviour to continue coding.

troubleshooting.question: How do I report a bug or request a feature?
troubleshooting.answer: Use the GitHub issues tracker at https://github.com/olivierfriard/BORIS/issues; the project also documents a 'how to report a bug' page.

nwb.function: Standard data format plus conversion/read-write APIs for neurophysiology

components.name: PyNWB
components.role: Python reference read/write API for the NWB 2.x format

components.name: NeuroConv
components.role: Converts ~50 proprietary neurophysiology formats to NWB; handles piecewise reading of large data, chunking and lossless compression, and temporal alignment of multiple streams

components.name: NWB GUIDE
components.role: Desktop app giving a no-code interface to NeuroConv

troubleshooting.question: Which API should I use for my language?
troubleshooting.answer: PyNWB for Python, MatNWB for MATLAB, AqNWB for C++. For R, Julia, Java or JavaScript, use a standard HDF5 reader — but note those readers are not aware of NWB schema details.

troubleshooting.question: Do I need to install nwb-schema separately?
troubleshooting.answer: No. The current schema always ships with the corresponding API, so end users do not need to interact with the nwb-schema repo.

troubleshooting.question: Can I read older NWB 1.x files?
troubleshooting.answer: PyNWB includes a pynwb/legacy module supporting NWB:N 1.0.x files from popular repositories such as the Allen Cell Types Atlas. For 1.0.x files from other sources results vary, particularly where files include custom data or are missing required fields. api-python is deprecated.

troubleshooting.question: NWB GUIDE install instructions are missing.
troubleshooting.answer: NWB GUIDE is in pre-release and under active development; the documented route is to clone the repository rather than install a release.

troubleshooting.question: Format-specific conversion dependencies fail in NeuroConv.
troubleshooting.answer: Per-format dependency install instructions live in the Conversion Examples Gallery, not the main install page.

verification.notes: Modelled as one entry with components because the source CSV uses NWB GUIDE, PyNWB and NeuroConv interchangeably across rows. Python/OS prerequisites not captured this pass — left null rather than guessed.
